note: Defaults shipped with stam. Override or extend any entry in STAM_HOME/registry.json; entries there replace these by key. null means unknown.
delegation: A missing capability is not a dead end: find an agent that has it with find_agents, or spawn one with spawn_agent, and delegate that part of the task.

opencode.description: OpenCode 2, run against stam's private OpenCode server.

codex.description: OpenAI Codex CLI: each agent runs its own Codex app-server with the Codex TUI attached.

prices.note: Public API prices in USD per million tokens, by model and token type, used to weight tokens when splitting a subscription window among agents (docs/cost-policy.md, Attribution). null means unverified: a null model weighs 1 per token, a null type uses the model's input price. Claude: Anthropic's API prices (cache write is the 5-minute rate; Haiku's is the card for prompts up to 100K tokens). Others: OpenRouter's public model list, 2026-10-11.

deep.description: Hard design, tricky debugging, and reviews where mistakes are expensive.

fast.description: Quick lookups, simple edits, and short-lived helper agents.

second-opinion.description: A cheap model from another company, for a second opinion or bulk simple tasks.

developer.description: One small, well-defined code change: implements it, tests it, and commits it on its own branch.
developer.brief:
Task: {{task}}

You work in {{cwd}}. Commit on the branch you were spawned on; don't create another. When the branch is ready, push it and open a pull request with `gh pr create`, naming your ITSA in the body; link the PR to your ITSA with `itsa_link`. Then `watch_pr` the PR, so its checks and reviews reach you. Then mail {{parent}} your branch and commits, the PR link, what changed, what you tested and the results, and anything you weren't sure about. Then set your ITSA to `in_review`, and stop. Never set it to done; whoever merges the PR does. If you're blocked, mail {{parent}} instead of guessing. Never mail the human; report to your parent.

reviewer.description: Reviews a change for bugs and risks before it merges; reports findings, doesn't edit the code.
reviewer.brief:
Review: {{task}}

Read the diff; your review is read-only, so don't run tests or edit the code. Watch the PR you review with `watch_pr` when it's open, so you hear its checks and any changes. When the review is of a PR, give your verdict with `gh pr review PR_NUMBER --comment --body "approve: SUMMARY"` (or `request_changes: SUMMARY`), then mail {{parent}} your verdict and findings when you're done.

reviewer-opus.description: Backup reviewer when Codex's window runs low.
reviewer-opus.brief:
Review: {{task}}

Read the diff; your review is read-only, so don't run tests or edit the code. Watch the PR you review with `watch_pr` when it's open, so you hear its checks and any changes. When the review is of a PR, give your verdict with `gh pr review PR_NUMBER --comment --body "approve: SUMMARY"` (or `request_changes: SUMMARY`), then mail {{parent}} your verdict and findings when you're done.

review-ring.description: Risky, cross-cutting, or security-sensitive changes: Codex and Opus review in rounds until they agree.

manager.description: Owns a bigger or uncertain change: splits it into small changes, spawns a developer for each and a reviewer, and reports the result.

coordinator.description: A manager for routine work that doesn't need judgment: splits clear tasks, spawns developers, and collects their results.

retro-steward.description: After a retro digest, drafts one proposal of instruction and template edits that answer open retro items, for the human to approve; applies it only after Approve.
retro-steward.brief:
{{task}}

You work in {{cwd}}. Mail {{parent}} when the proposal waits on your user, when it is approved and committed, or when there is nothing to propose.

cos.description: The chief of staff: schedules and manages the other agents. Spawning it makes it the chief of staff; at most one is active.

advisor.description: A powerful second mind for a hard decision, design, or problem; answers and advises, doesn't build.
